item.title: Pedal Power on a Budget: Our Adventure Finding the Perfect Second-Hand Bike in Germany with Deutschlandticket
item.description: When we first moved to Germany, settling into our new life was an adventure in itself. From navigating the bureaucracy to learning the local customs, every day brought something new. One of the first things we realized, especially living in a city, was the absolute necessity of a bicycle. It’s not just a hobby here; for many, it’s a primary mode of transport – practical, environmentally friendly, and a fantastic way to explore. But new bikes can be incredibly expensive, especially for a family just starting out. That’s when we embarked on our quest for second-hand bikes, a journey that taught us a lot about German resourcefulness and the incredible utility of the Deutschlandticket.

item.title: Romantic Road Guide | Bavaria’s Most Beautiful Route with Deutschlandticket and a Stroller (2026)
item.description:
What is the Romantic Road?
#

Romantische Straße — Germany’s most famous tourist route. Stretching approximately 460 km from Würzburg to Füssen, this route is filled with medieval towns, city walls, castles, and Alpine views.

But we didn’t do this route like typical tourists.

We did it with the Deutschlandticket, two children (aged 1 and 5), and a double stroller. We learned firsthand which cities are stroller-accessible, which stations have elevators, and which cafes are kid-friendly.

item.title: Deutschlandticket Day Trips from Munich | Bavaria with Kids (2026)
item.description: For 49 EUR per month you can take all local and regional trains across Germany. From Munich to Füssen, Garmisch, Salzburg, Starnberg Lake — routes we tested with two kids aged 1 and 5 and a double stroller.
